description:
A `case`/dispatch arm whose pattern is a struct (`%Box{}`, `%Range{}`) is ENTERED
by a plain map, because the arm's test is the structural map shape rather than the
nominal tag. The map then fails during struct field extraction instead of taking
the miss edge.

## Minimal repro -- no protocol, no Enumerable

    defmodule Box do defstruct [:value] end

    fn classify(v) do
      case v do
        %Box{value: x} -> {:box, x}
        _ -> :other
      end
    end

    fn main() do
      dbg(classify(%Box{value: 7}))
      dbg(classify(%{1 => :one}))
    end

    $ fz2 interp
    {:box, 7}
    fz2 interp: backend executable 4 function 31 entry 1 step evaluation failed:
      match_error: expected struct Box

`run` and the AOT binary both print `{:box, 7}` then
`match_error: ... halted through a fault trap`.

ELIXIR answers `{:box, 7}` then `:other` -- a plain map must MISS the struct
clause and fall to the wildcard.

## Through protocol dispatch it needs only a TWO-member union

With `fn counted(value), do: Enumerable.count(value)`:

    Range alone   => {:ok, 5}
    map alone     => {:ok, 2}
    List | Map    => {{:ok, 3}, {:ok, 2}}        all fine
    Range | Map   => match_error: expected struct Range

`fixtures2/behavior/enumerable_protocol_dispatch.fz` (receiver List|Range|Map,
expected `{{:ok, 3}, {:ok, 5}, {:ok, 2}}`) is deferred on all three lanes for
this. Its failure has advanced one step PAST the match_error: with the
`# defer.*` lines removed it gives
`backend dispatch callsite in executable 8 missed an exhaustive dispatch`
(src/ir_interp/backend.rs:712) on interp, and
`compiler2_unreachable_control: halted through a fault trap` on run/build.

Fixing the three-way case may need both the nominal-tag ordering AND the reason
the three-arm dispatch is left non-exhaustive. The two-way case is the clean,
isolated signal -- fix that first.

Root-cause premise holds in code: `World::struct_value_ty` (world.rs:1803) and
`Region::Type` dispatch (jobs/backend.rs:2206, jobs/native.rs:3072,
native_codegen/receive.rs:611).

## What the old ticket got wrong

It claimed `fixtures2/behavior/membership_operator.fz` was still deferred on this
and printed only four of six expected lines. That fixture carries NO defer lines
at HEAD, passes 3/3 in the matrix, and prints all six booleans. Both of its
"Direct repro" bullets are dead as written. Only enumerable_protocol_dispatch
remains, and its interp symptom has CHANGED from `match_error: expected struct
Range` to `missed an exhaustive dispatch`.

## Checks

- The `%Box{}`-then-wildcard repro returns `:other` for a plain map on interp,
  run and build.
- `Enumerable.count` over a `Range|Map` receiver returns
  `{{:ok, 5}, {:ok, 2}}` on all three paths.
- Remove the three `# defer.*` lines from
  fixtures2/behavior/enumerable_protocol_dispatch.fz; its three matrix lanes pass
  (they are ignored today).
- Full lib + matrix green.
title: Struct dispatch tests map shape before nominal tag: a plain map enters a struct arm and match_errors on all three paths
